answer_1.quote: We propose an algorithm to sample text nonautoregressively from a conditional or unconditional LM trained to perform any language generation task—translation, summarization, dialog, prompt completion—while controlling for multiple constraints.
answer_1.outputs: Generated continuations, translations, keyword‑constrained sentences, and summaries

answer_2.quote: We evaluate the generated samples along three dimensions, (1) Constraint Satisfaction measured using external evaluators, (2) Fluency, measured by mean perplexity of the continuations measured using GPT2-XL, (3) Diversity, measured by computing the mean number of distinct n‑grams in each set of samples, normalized by the length of text.

answer_3.quote: Fluency, measured by mean perplexity of the continuations measured using GPT2-XL.

answer_4.quote: We also perform human evaluation in an A/B testing setup with the best performing baseline (DExperts in our case). For each sample, we ask 3 annotators to compare and rank candidates from our approach and the baseline on constraint satisfaction, topicality and fluency.
answer_4.guideline: Annotators compare pairs of outputs and rank them according to (1) constraint satisfaction, (2) topicality (coherence with prompt), and (3) fluency (grammatical correctness).
